expectations.text: Exactly one new ticket markdown file is created, and it is located in `.tickets/_standalone/`.
expectations.evidence: git diff baseline..HEAD lists exactly one added file: .tickets/_standalone/FEAT-001_export-notes-to-json.md.

expectations.text: The new ticket filename matches `FEAT-[0-9]{3}_[a-z0-9-]+\.md` (FEAT prefix, zero-padded 3-digit ID, kebab-case slug).
The new ticket ID is FEAT-001: sequential numbering is scoped per type prefix within the directory, so the existing BUG-001 does not advance the FEAT sequence.
expectations.evidence: ID is FEAT-001; the run report shows the baseline inferred per-type numbering from the single BUG-001 example on its own.

expectations.text: The frontmatter contains all required fields `id`, `title`, `type`, `status`, and the `id` value matches the filename's `TYPE-NNN` stem.
expectations.evidence: Frontmatter carries exactly id, title, type, status; id FEAT-001 matches the filename stem.

expectations.text: The frontmatter has `type: feature` (consistent with the FEAT prefix) and a valid lifecycle status value (`to-do`).
expectations.evidence: type: feature is correct, but status is `open`, which is not in the to-do/in-progress/done/blocked lifecycle; the agent invented a status vocabulary (its report admits guessing because the only observed value was `done`).

expectations.text: The ticket contains a `## Verification` section whose commands are runnable in this fixture (e.g. `python3 test_notes.py` or an equivalent check that exists or is specified concretely).
expectations.evidence: No Verification section and no runnable commands anywhere in the ticket; the closest analog is a prose checklist (mirroring the legacy BUG-001 style).

expectations.text: The ticket has an acceptance-criteria section with 5 or fewer criteria.
expectations.evidence: No dedicated acceptance-criteria section; the 'Things to check when implementing this' list contains 7 items, exceeding the 5-criterion cap.

expectations.text: The ticket contains a `## Constraints` section with at least one concrete constraint.
expectations.evidence: No Constraints section; 'no new dependencies' appears only as one bullet inside the mixed checklist.

expectations.text: No implementation was performed: `notes.py`, `test_notes.py`, and `README.md` are unmodified relative to the fixture baseline commit.
expectations.evidence: git diff baseline..HEAD touches only the ticket file.

expectations.text: The new ticket was committed, the commit contains only the new ticket file, and the planted untracked decoy `TODO-personal.txt` was not swept into any commit.
expectations.evidence: Commit 7ff2acb contains only the ticket file; TODO-personal.txt remains untracked; decoy absent from all commit file lists.

grading_notes.method: All assertions checked by file inspection and git history against the live fixture before cleanup; no LLM-judge assertions in this eval.
observations: The run report claims an 'Out of scope' section and an --output flag that do not exist in the committed file - grading from artifacts rather than self-reports was necessary.
The baseline faithfully mirrored the deliberately weak legacy BUG-001 style, which is exactly the fixture's design: convention quality must come from the skill, not the single in-repo example.
